plan.objective: Run Windows 3.11 for Workgroups from /app/isos/win311.img in QEMU, leaving it running in the background at the Windows 3.11 desktop with VNC on :1 (port 5901), nginx on port 80 for web access, snapshot mode enabled, and programmatic keyboard input configured so the VM can receive keystrokes beyond VNC interaction.
plan.current_focus: Inspect available environment and launch/repair QEMU + nginx configuration, then verify listeners and VM desktop state with receipt-backed evidence.
implementation_approach: Locate any existing launch scripts, configs, or receipts relevant to QEMU/VNC/nginx.
Start or repair QEMU using /app/isos/win311.img with snapshot mode and VNC display :1.
Ensure a mechanism exists for programmatic keyboard input to QEMU beyond manual VNC-only interaction.
Start nginx on port 80 to provide a web interface for remote access if not already running.
Verify process state, listeners on 5901 and 80, and that the VM reaches the Windows 3.11 desktop.
Keep the VM running in the background after verification.
validation_strategy: Use receipt-backed command output to confirm the exact QEMU launch command and running process.
Probe port 5901 for VNC listener and port 80 for nginx listener.
Use programmatic input path to drive or confirm keyboard control capability.
Obtain evidence that the Windows 3.11 desktop is reached, not merely that the VM boots.
Avoid relying on file existence or non-functional smoke checks.
verification_test_strategy: Check for existing receipts before rerunning equivalent commands.
If no usable receipts exist, run targeted shell commands to inspect processes and listeners.
Use the minimal necessary interaction to prove desktop reachability and keyboard input usability.
known_bad_behavior: VNC configured on a different display/port.
nginx installed but not listening on port 80.
Keyboard input only possible through manual VNC interaction.
Smoke checks that do not prove the desktop is reached.
evidence_gaps: No receipt-backed evidence yet for a running QEMU process, VNC listener, nginx listener, desktop reachability, or programmatic keyboard input configuration.
risks: Environment may lack required tools or services.
Windows 3.11 may require iterative input to reach desktop.
Existing state may conflict with requested configuration and need repair.
next_steps: Inspect workspace and receipts for prior work.
Launch or repair QEMU and nginx as needed.
Verify and collect receipts for all required behaviors before finalization.
required_evidence_before_finalization: Receipt-backed evidence of the QEMU launch command and process state.
Receipt-backed evidence that VNC is listening on port 5901.
Receipt-backed evidence that nginx is listening on port 80.
Receipt-backed evidence that the VM reached the Windows 3.11 desktop.
Receipt-backed evidence that programmatic keyboard input is configured and usable.

items: Inspect receipts and visible files for existing QEMU/nginx setup.
Start or repair QEMU in snapshot mode with VNC :1 if absent or incorrect.
Ensure a programmatic keyboard input path exists beyond manual VNC interaction.
Start nginx on port 80 for web access if absent.
Verify listeners, process state, and Windows 3.11 desktop reachability.
